findings.where: First screen (desktop and phone), the nav and the space under the supporting line; and the whole page
findings.fault: There is no way to reach Mark anywhere on the page. The email address is not shown, there is no mailto link, the nav has no Contact item, and the pad-yellow 'address strip' that the palette describes never appears. The parts map lists no contact part. The first screen ends on the supporting paragraph and has no action at all.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has decided Mark is worth an email but finds no address to write to. The founder would object too: the brief requires one direct, personal way to reach him, with the address shown, and requires one action on the first screen.

findings.where: Motion sketch section, the full-width lavender panel
findings.fault: The motion sketch sits on a saturated lavender ground that is in neither the palette nor the brief. It is the loudest colour on the page and draws the eye from everything around it. Blue link text then sits on the purple, a third hue next to the house blue.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief says the house blue and grey are the only ink, with one soft ground and one pale yellow at most. A lilac block reads as playful, not refined counsel's paper, and makes the tile look less disciplined than its own palette notes claim.

findings.where: Article specimen, the 'Download' link 'Streamlining the PPP Process: Meeting the 'Abundance' Challenge'
findings.fault: The PDF link is styled as a working download, with an underline in the link colour and the label 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF'. Its target is '#', so clicking it goes nowhere.
findings.who_objects: A reader who wants Mark's lecture and gets nothing. The research brief calls the article and the PDF list 'the product', and this is the depth the page offers after the first look.

findings.where: Article specimen, the subhead 'So, what are the key 'chapter topics'?' and the 'Download' heading
findings.fault: The subheads are set in a heavy, wide black grotesque. That is a third face, outside the stated pair (Newsreader 500 for subheads, Public Sans for labels), and it clashes with the light serif voice and the bold serif title above.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for serious, refined type with nothing 'in-your-face techy'. The stated type pair also says what Angélique will use. A block-letter subhead in every article would read as a different publication.

findings.fault: The four swatches all do the same job but each has a different shape: a square-cornered box, a rounded box, an ellipse, and a box with a thick blue border. Only the yellow swatch has the blue edge, so it reads as the selected option in a picker.
findings.who_objects: The founder, reading the tile as a spec. The varied shapes suggest corner radius and border meanings the direction does not have (it says 'square at every corner'), and the blue-edged swatch looks like a selection where nothing can be chosen.

findings.where: First screen, the supporting line under Mark's heading
findings.fault: The first screen says what Mark does and for whom, but not where he works. No region or base country is given, so the reader has to guess whether he works in their region.
findings.who_objects: A procurement reader at a development bank, who selects advisors by region of experience and wants to know at a glance that Mark has worked where they work.
